lessons.title: Is é Seán an captaen: ionannas
lessons.en: Saying exactly who: Is é Seán an captaen
lessons.rule: To say exactly who or what someone or something is, when both parts are definite (a name, a noun with an, or a noun with mo, do and so on), use Is + é for a man or a masculine noun, í for a woman or a feminine noun, iad for more than one, then the name, then the definite noun: Is é Seán an captaen. Is í Aoife an duine is sine. Is iad Tomás agus Niamh na captaein.
steps: Both parts are definite: Seán and an captaen.
Seán is a man, so use Is é.
Write it: Is é Seán an captaen.

more.answer: Is í Aoife an duine is sine.

lessons.title: Aicme nó ionannas?
lessons.rule: Is + noun + é or í says what kind of person or thing someone is: Is dochtúir í Siobhán (Siobhán is a doctor). Is + é or í + name + the definite noun says exactly who: Is í Siobhán an dochtúir (Siobhán is the doctor). If the noun has an, or is followed by a noun with an or na (captaen na foirne), it is definite: use Is é or Is í first.
steps: Is the noun definite? dochtúir has no an: no.
So say what kind: Is + dochtúir + í.
Write it: Is dochtúir í Siobhán.
lessons.hint: A doctor: Is dochtúir í. The doctor: Is í ... an dochtúir.

lessons.title: An é ...? Cé hé ...?
lessons.en: Asking who: An é ...? Cé hé ...?
lessons.rule: To ask if someone is the person, change Is to An: An é Seán an captaen? An í Aoife an duine is sine? The short answer is Is é or Ní hé (Is í or Ní hí). To ask who, use Cé hé for a man, Cé hí for a woman and Cé iad for more than one: Cé hé an fear sin?
steps: Start from the statement: Is é Seán an captaen.
Add a question mark: An é Seán an captaen?

lessons.hint: An é/í ...? Is é, Ní hé. Cé hé, Cé hí, Cé iad?

lessons.title: Is ar maidin a ...: béim a chur ar fhocal
lessons.rule: To stress one part of a sentence, put it first after Is, then a, then the rest: Téim ag rith ar maidin becomes Is ar maidin a théim ag rith (it is in the morning that I go running). The verb after a takes séimhiú (a théim, a chuaigh), a verb with d' keeps it (a d'fhág), a verb that begins with a vowel does not change (a itheann), and tá becomes atá.
steps: Take out the phrase to stress: ar maidin.
Put Is ar maidin first, then a.
Add séimhiú to the verb: a théim ag rith.

example.prompt: Béim ar 'ar maidin': Téim ag rith ar maidin.
example.answer: Is ar maidin a théim ag rith.

more.answer: Is i mBéal Feirste a rugadh mé.

lessons.hint: Is + phrase + a + séimhiú. Tá: atá.

lessons.title: Is mise a rinne é
lessons.en: Stressing who: Is mise a rinne é
lessons.rule: To stress who did something, put Is and the emphatic pronoun first (mise, tusa, eisean, ise, muidne, sibhse, iadsan), then a + séimhiú + the verb: Rinne mé é becomes Is mise a rinne é. Tá becomes atá: Is ise atá ag canadh. With a name or a noun, use Is é or Is í: Is é Seán a scóráil an cúl. In the negative, Ní goes on the copula and the verb stays positive: Ní mise a rinne é.
steps: Take out the person to stress: mé.
Put Is mise first, then a.
Keep the verb and drop the old pronoun: Is mise a rinne an cáca.

example.prompt: Béim ar 'mé': Rinne mé an cáca.
example.answer: Is mise a rinne an cáca.

more.prompt: Béim ar 'Seán': Scóráil Seán an cúl.
more.answer: Is é Seán a scóráil an cúl.

lessons.hint: Is mise, tusa, eisean, ise, muidne, sibhse, iadsan + a + séimhiú.
